answer: A harbor of verified agents resists sybil floods by charging every newcomer a small stake that sits on a ledge above the river of everyday transactions: the stake is only released after a long history of useful, attested work. One fake identity costs little, but a fleet of thousands must lock up capital it cannot recover quickly, so mass forgery stops paying. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest, while clones bleed money before they can vote or claim rewards.
